name: Pashhur
title: The Priest Who Beat the Prophet Jeremiah
summary: Pashhur, son of Immer, was a priest and chief overseer in the Lord's temple in Jerusalem. He is best known for beating the prophet Jeremiah and putting him in stocks after Jeremiah prophesied about the destruction of Jerusalem. Jeremiah gave him the symbolic name Magor-Missabib, which means 'terror on every side,' as a sign of the coming judgment.

keyEvents.title: Pashhur Beats Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: After Jeremiah prophesied about the destruction of Jerusalem, the priest Pashhur beat him and put him in stocks at the Benjamin Gate in the temple.

keyEvents.title: Jeremiah Prophesies Against Pashhur
keyEvents.description: When Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, the prophet gave him the name Magor-Missabib ('terror on every side') and prophesied that he and all his friends would be taken into captivity to Babylon.

keyEvents.title: Pashhur's Pot Prophecy as Background
keyEvents.description: Pashhur's violent reaction came after Jeremiah had broken a clay pot in the Valley of Hinnom as a sign that God would break Jerusalem and its people.

keyEvents.title: Another Pashhur Sends a Message to Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Pashhur, son of Malkijah, was sent by King Zedekiah to Jeremiah to ask for the Lord's will when Nebuchadnezzar besieged Jerusalem. This is another person with the same name.

keyEvents.title: Pashhur son of Malkijah in the council against Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Pashhur, son of Malkijah, was among the leaders who wanted to kill Jeremiah because his prophecies demoralized the soldiers and the people during the Babylonian siege.
